transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I guess I'm here because... well, it started a few weeks ago, maybe a month, when I noticed the dispatch system at work was acting up. I drive for the city transit, you see, and I've been doing this for a while, so I know how the system is supposed to work. But recently, dispatch and the compliance office... they've been tracking my route changes. And not just the normal way, like where they check to make sure you're on schedule. It's through the computer system, like they're logging every single time I brake or turn a minute late. And then there are these little comments on the radio. They think they're being subtle, but I hear them. They'll say things like, "Watch the turns on Route 4," which is my route, or they'll click the mic twice when I pass a certain intersection. I tried talking to my supervisor about it, and he just brushed it off, saying it's just normal oversight, you know, standard procedure for all drivers. But it's not. I can tell. It's different for me. And it's not just management, either. I've noticed certain other drivers... the ones who always take their breaks near my bus... they're reporting on me. They watch what I do and report back to compliance. It's exhausting, honestly, having to be on guard every single shift, wondering what they're logging next.
Do you think there's a specific reason why they're doing this to you?

I really... I don't know. And honestly, that is exactly what drives me absolutely crazy about all of this. I mean, if they just came out and said, hey, you did this one thing wrong, or we're auditing you because of this specific incident, then fine. I could handle that. I could address it. But I have racked my brain, doctor, I really have. I've gone back through every single shift report in my head, just sitting in my apartment after work, going over and over the last few months. 

I keep thinking, was it that time in October when I had to detour around the water main break on 5th Avenue? But no, dispatch explicitly approved that over the radio, so it can't be that. Or maybe it's because I'm one of the only drivers in my shift group who actually does the full pre-trip inspection, like checking the tire pressure and the air brakes before every single run, exactly the way we were taught. Maybe it makes the older drivers look bad because they just breeze through it, so they complained about me? But even that doesn't explain why compliance would use the computer system to track my braking patterns. 

I just don't know. I have my associate's degree, I'm a professional, I'm not some kid just joyriding a city vehicle. I take my route seriously. But I can't pinpoint a single, logical trigger for why I'm the one being singled out like this. It's just this massive missing piece of the puzzle, and it makes it so much more exhausting because I can't even defend myself. How do you defend yourself when you don't even know what you supposedly did to warrant this kind of 24/7 surveillance? So, no, I don't know the reason. I just know it's happening.
Do you ever think that maybe they're not actually tracking you or reporting on you?

I mean... I know what you're asking. You're asking if maybe I'm just making a big deal out of nothing, right? Like maybe I'm just stressed out or misinterpreting things. My sister said something similar when I tried to explain it to her last week. She was like, 'Oh, you're just tired, they track everyone's bus.' And I get why you'd ask that. I really do. If I were sitting where you are, listening to me, I might wonder the same thing. But... no. I don't think that. Because I'm not stupid, doctor. I know the difference between standard fleet management and what's happening to me. 

Like I said before, I know they say it's just normal oversight, just standard procedure. But it's the computer system, you know? It's the way they use it. The telematics on the buses, they're designed to flag major things—hard braking, speeding, going way off route. But for me, it's every tiny little route change. If I have to swing wide because a delivery truck is parked in the bike lane on 3rd Street, which happens literally every Tuesday and Thursday morning, they log it. And then the radio comments... it's not just regular dispatch chatter. It's targeted. When they say, 'Watch the turns on Route 4,' they know I'm listening. They know I know what they mean. 

And the other drivers... I can't just ignore that. You don't just happen to take your coffee break at the exact same turnaround point I'm at, three days in a row, when your route is on the other side of the district. It doesn't make logistical sense. I've looked at the schedules. I know how the shifts are structured. They are going out of their way to be where I am, to watch me, and to report back to compliance. So, no, I don't think I'm imagining it. I don't think it's just a misunderstanding. I'm here because they are tracking me, through the computers, through the radio, through the other drivers. I can tell. I just... I know it's real, even if people keep trying to tell me it's just normal oversight.
Have you ever felt like you were being targeted or watched like this before?

No... no, I haven't. Not like this. I mean, sure, when I was in college getting my associate's, I had a professor who I felt graded me a little too harshly, like she was always watching to see if I'd mess up a citation or something, but that was just... that was just school, you know? That was normal pressure. This is entirely different. I've never experienced anything on this level before. 

It really started to become obvious to me... well, I'd say the tracking through the computer system and those specific radio comments, they've felt incredibly clear to me for about the past two months. I can trace it back to the beginning of the new quarter. It was a Tuesday, I remember, because it was raining, and the wipers on bus 402 always stick when it rains. I was dealing with the wipers, trying to keep my schedule, and that's when I first noticed the telematics system blinking differently when I tapped the brakes. And then the dispatcher—it was Dave on duty that day—clicked the mic twice. At first, I thought, 'Okay, maybe it's a glitch, maybe Dave just bumped the button.' But then it happened the next day. And the day after that. 

So for the last two months, it's just been building and building. Every week, it's like they add a new layer to it. First the computer, then the radio, then the other drivers showing up at my turnaround spots. It's like this net they've been slowly tightening around me for eight solid weeks. Before that? Nothing. I was just doing my job, driving my route, going home. I had a great record. I still have a great record, technically, if they'd just look at the actual driving and not whatever it is they're logging now. But yeah, to answer your question, this level of surveillance, this coordinated effort... it's completely new. Just the last two months of my life turning into this constant, exhausting watch.
Have you had any similar thoughts or feelings of being watched or targeted outside of your job?

Outside of my job? Like... at the grocery store or my apartment? No. No, not really. I mean, when I go to the grocery store over on Washington—which I usually do on Thursday evenings, by the way, because it's less crowded and I can just get my produce and get out—I don't feel like the cashiers are looking at me funny or the store manager is following me down the aisle. My apartment complex is quiet, too. I know my neighbors, mostly just to wave to, but nobody is peeking through my blinds. It's just... normal life stuff out there. 

But the problem is, doctor, I can't even enjoy that normal life stuff anymore. Because even when I'm sitting on my couch, trying to just eat dinner or watch a show, my brain is just spinning and spinning about work. I can't let it go because of how intense it is. I mean, I’m here, sitting in this chair talking to you, because dispatch and compliance have been tracking my route changes through the computer system, and it just consumes everything I do. I go home and I just obsess over those little comments on the radio from my shift. I replay them over and over in my head, trying to figure out what their end game is. 

And it's incredibly isolating. It really is. Because even when people say it’s just normal oversight—like my sister, or even if I tried to explain it to a union rep, they just give me this look like I'm overreacting to standard fleet management. But I'm the one in the driver's seat. I can tell certain drivers are reporting on me, showing up at my turnaround spots, watching my breaks. So, no, it's not happening at the grocery store or the laundromat. It's just them. It's just at work. But honestly, it doesn't even need to happen anywhere else, because what they're doing to me on the clock is already bleeding into every single second of my day.
Do you ever have any doubts that you're being tracked or targeted by your employer?

Doubts? I mean, I feel like we sort of just touched on this when you asked if I thought I was misinterpreting things. But to be absolutely, one hundred percent clear with you... no. I really do not have doubts. And I know you probably have to ask that, I know it is your job to see if I am wavering or second-guessing myself or whatever, but you have to understand the sheer volume of what I am dealing with. If it was just one isolated incident, maybe. Like, if it was only the telematics being weird, I could maybe convince myself that the sensors were just overly sensitive to the bumps on 3rd Street. 

But I am here, sitting in this exact chair talking to you, because dispatch and compliance have been tracking my route changes through the computer system, and it never just stops there. It is the computer, plus those little comments on the radio that I mentioned, all layered on top of each other day after day. And even when people keep trying to tell me it is just normal oversight—which is what management always hides behind, by the way, they just say it is standard fleet management—I know it is not. I can tell certain drivers are reporting on me. I can literally see it in the way they position their buses at the turnaround spots and how they watch me on my breaks. You do not just get that kind of coordination by accident. 

So how could I doubt it? If you were in my driver seat and every time you had to swing wide around a parked delivery truck, the computer logged it and dispatch immediately keyed the mic to make a targeted comment about your steering... you would not doubt it either. You would know exactly what was happening. I do not have the luxury of doubting it because I am living in it every single shift. It is a very real, very coordinated effort by compliance, dispatch, and the other drivers. Honestly, my only doubt is about what they actually plan to do with all this information they are collecting on me, not whether or not it is happening.
Do you think the comments on the radio or the actions of the other drivers are related to anything specific you've done or anything about you personally?

Well, see, that’s… that’s the million-dollar question, isn't it? That’s the exact thing that keeps me up at night, just staring at the ceiling, trying to figure out the *why* of it all. I sit there and I rack my brain trying to think if I made someone mad, you know? Did I cut off a supervisor in the depot? Did I complain too loudly about the new scheduling software in the breakroom? I mean, I’ve always been a good driver, I follow the rules, I did well when I was getting my associate's, so I know how to follow instructions and be a professional. But I must have crossed some invisible line with someone high up, because... well, like I’ve been saying, I’m here because dispatch and compliance have been tracking my route changes through the computer system, and it is just so incredibly specific to me. 

If it wasn't personal, why would they dedicate so much time and so many resources to my bus? Every little deviation, every time I have to swing wide for a garbage truck or take a parallel street because of construction, it gets logged. And then come those little comments on the radio. They are tailored to me. They know exactly what they're doing when they say them. And I know I probably sound like a broken record to you, but it’s just so endlessly frustrating when I try to explain this and people just brush it off. Even when people say it’s just normal oversight, or standard fleet management, or whatever corporate buzzword they want to use to make it sound okay... I know the difference. I've been driving long enough to know what normal looks like. I can tell certain drivers are reporting on me. 

I see them at the turnaround spots, doing things that make no sense for their own routes. Like, earlier this week, I had to take a slight detour around a stalled car—a totally necessary route change for safety—and suddenly there's another driver from a completely different zone just sitting there at my next stop, idling, watching me fill out my logbook. You don't just do that unless you've been given orders to keep tabs on someone. So, did I do something specific? I honestly don't know what it could possibly be. I really don't. But they are absolutely treating it like it's personal, building this whole elaborate case against me with the compliance logs and the informants, and I just can't get a straight answer out of anyone about what I supposedly did to trigger all of this.
Do you think the people tracking you at work are also watching you outside of work?

Well, like I was saying before when we talked about the grocery store and my apartment complex... physically? No. I don't think they are. I really don't think dispatch is parking an unmarked car across the street from my building or following me to the laundromat on the weekends to see what detergent I buy. But... and this is the thing that is just so incredibly hard to explain to people who aren't living it... they don't really need to follow me home. They just don't. Because what they do to me on the clock is so heavy and so constant that I carry it right through my front door anyway. 

I know I keep repeating myself today, and I know you're probably taking notes right now thinking I'm just stuck on a loop, but I am literally only here in this office because dispatch and compliance have been tracking my route changes through the computer system, and making those little comments on the radio that I told you about. It is relentless. And even when people say it’s just normal oversight, which is what everyone always wants to fall back on to make me sound crazy, I know what I'm seeing. I can tell certain drivers are reporting on me. I see them at the turnarounds, I see them idling where they shouldn't be. 

So when I go home, lock my door, and sit on my couch to try and eat dinner... I'm alone, sure. Nobody is looking through my blinds. But my brain is just spinning and spinning, replaying the whole shift, trying to decode what the other drivers were writing down about me or what dispatch meant when they clicked the mic. I can't even watch a movie without thinking about the compliance logs. So, no, they aren't physically watching me outside of work, but they might as well be, because what they're doing to me on the road has completely taken over every single minute of my life outside of work anyway.
Can you think of any other reason why dispatch and the other drivers might be acting this way towards you, other than that they are intentionally tracking you?

I mean, I’ve tried. I really, really have tried to come up with another explanation, because believe me, living with this is exhausting. I’ve sat there and thought, okay, maybe there’s a new city ordinance about fuel efficiency that I missed the memo on, and that’s why they care so much about every single time I brake or turn. Or maybe the other drivers are just taking their breaks at weird times because their own schedules got messed up by the new software. I’ve tried to rationalize it like that, I really have. 

But then I go back to work, and the reality of it just hits me in the face all over again. I’m here because dispatch and compliance have been tracking my route changes through the computer system, and then there are those little comments on the radio that just line up too perfectly with whatever I just did. It’s too coordinated to be a coincidence or a new policy. And even when people say it’s just normal oversight, or they try to tell me that fleet management is just cracking down on everyone... I know that’s not true. I can see the difference. I can tell certain drivers are reporting on me, specifically. 

Like, if it was just normal oversight, why would that one guy on the 42 route always happen to be idling at the exact intersection where I have to swing wide to avoid the potholes on 5th? He doesn't even drive that zone! He has no business being there unless he's logging my movements. So, sure, I've tried to think of other reasons. I've tried to tell myself I'm just stressed or reading too much into standard procedures. But the sheer amount of effort they are putting into monitoring my bus... there is just no other logical explanation. They are intentionally tracking me, and they are using the other drivers to do it.
Do you think it's possible that there could be another explanation for the things that are happening to you at work, other than that you are being intentionally tracked?

I feel like we are just going in circles here, doctor. I mean, didn't you basically just ask me that? I know you are trying to do your job and get me to see some other side of this, to find some magical alternative explanation that makes all this go away. And like I just said, I really wish there was one. I wish I could sit here and tell you that it is all just a big misunderstanding. But I can't do that, because I am the one living it every single day. I am the one sitting in that driver seat for eight, ten hours a day. 

Look, the whole reason I am here, sitting in this chair talking to you right now, is because dispatch and compliance have been tracking my route changes through the computer system. That is the reality of the situation. And then there are those little comments on the radio that follow perfectly with what they are tracking. They aren't just random static or standard dispatch chatter. And I know everybody wants to tell me it is just normal oversight. They want to package it up as fleet management or quality control so I will just be quiet and go back to work and stop making a fuss. But I am not stupid. I know how to do my job, I have my associate's degree, I know how these systems operate, and I can tell certain drivers are reporting on me. I can literally see it happening with my own two eyes. 

So no, I really don't think it is possible there is another explanation. Because when you have the computer data, the radio comments, and the other drivers acting as informants, what else could it possibly be? You can't just explain away all those pieces coming together to target one person. It just doesn't work like that, and honestly, it is so incredibly exhausting having to defend what I know is happening to me over and over again.
Do you think there's any possibility that your belief about being tracked is not based on real events?

Not based on real events? I... I mean, wow. I know you have to ask that, because of the type of doctor you are, but... no. No, absolutely not. How could it not be based on real events when it is happening right in front of me, every single shift? I feel like I'm just screaming into a void here. 

I know I keep saying this, but I really need you to understand that I’m only here because dispatch and compliance have been tracking my route changes through the computer system. That is a real, physical system. It’s software. It logs data. That’s a real event! And the little comments on the radio—I am hearing them with my own two ears through the speaker on my dashboard. I'm not making up the audio, they are actually pressing the button and speaking into the microphone to let me know they see what I'm doing. 

And look, I know everyone’s go-to excuse is that it’s just normal oversight. My supervisor, the union rep, everybody just waves their hands and says, 'Oh, it’s just normal oversight, they do it to everybody, don't worry about it.' But they don't do it to everybody. They just don't. I can tell certain drivers are reporting on me. I see them. I watch them watching me. If none of this was real, why would the other drivers be involved? Why would they be idling in my zones where they have absolutely no business being? 

It just... it really hurts, honestly, to be asked if this isn't real. Because my entire life is being consumed by this. I wouldn't put myself through this kind of stress, I wouldn't be sitting in this office taking time out of my day and paying co-pays if this wasn't based on concrete, actual things happening at my job. It is exhausting to constantly have my reality questioned. So, no. It's real. The computer tracking is real, the radio comments are real, the drivers acting as informants—it is all completely real, whether anyone else wants to admit it or not.
Do you think it's possible that your interpretation of the events at work might be incorrect?

Incorrect? My interpretation? Doctor, I... I don't even know how many different ways I can say this. It feels like you're just asking me the same question over and over again, just dressing it up in different words. First it was 'are there other reasons,' then 'is there another explanation,' then 'is it not real,' and now 'is my interpretation incorrect.' It’s like you’re waiting for me to just break down and say, 'Oh, you're right, doctor, silly me, I just imagined the whole thing!' But I can't do that. I won't do that, because that would be a lie.

I mean, let's really look at what you're asking me. You're asking if I'm somehow misinterpreting the fact that dispatch and compliance have been tracking my route changes through the computer system. How do you misinterpret data? How do you misinterpret a system that is literally designed to monitor location and speed and stops? It’s not like I’m looking at a cloud and saying it looks like a dog. I’m looking at a digital footprint of my entire workday that they are scrutinizing. And then, right on the heels of that, there are those little comments on the radio. It’s not just one comment, or two comments, it’s a pattern. It’s a continuous, ongoing commentary that perfectly aligns with the route changes they just tracked. How do you misinterpret someone keying the mic and making a specific remark about a turn I just made three seconds ago? 

And I know, I know what you're going to say, because it's what everyone says. Even when people say it’s just normal oversight, or that I'm just being sensitive to the new management style, or whatever excuse they want to use this week... it doesn't change what I see. I can tell certain drivers are reporting on me. I can see them. I can see the way they look at me in the breakroom, the way they pull out their phones when I walk by, the way they just happen to be parked on my route. You don't misinterpret that kind of coordinated effort. You just don't. 

So, to answer your question... no. I don't think my interpretation is incorrect. I think my interpretation is the only one that actually fits all the facts. And it’s incredibly frustrating that I have to keep defending my own reality to you, to my supervisor, to everyone. I’m not crazy, doctor. I’m just observant. And I am paying the price for noticing what they are doing to me.
Do you think the people tracking you believe they have a legitimate reason to do so?

Well... I mean, I guess in their own twisted way, they probably do. Or at least, that is what they tell themselves so they can sleep at night. Because, like I have brought up before, whenever anyone talks about this, even when people say it is just normal oversight, they act like they are just doing their jobs. They use all these corporate buzzwords. They probably tell themselves that they are just monitoring efficiency or keeping an eye on the fleet, like it is some noble company initiative to make sure the routes are optimized or whatever excuse they come up with for the higher-ups. 

But there is a huge, massive difference between normal oversight and what they are actually doing to me day in and day out. Because... and I know I sound like a broken record, but it is the absolute truth, I am here because dispatch and compliance have been tracking my route changes through the computer system in a way that is entirely, obsessively focused on me. It is not just some passive dot on a screen for them. It is active surveillance. And those little comments on the radio... do they think that is legitimate? Do they think it is professional to press the button and make these snide, coded little remarks about my exact location for the whole grid to hear? They probably think it is a game. They probably think it is funny to mess with my head while I am just trying to do my job safely and get through my shift without having a nervous breakdown. 

And as for the other drivers... I really do not know what they believe. Maybe management offered them better shifts, or maybe they just want to suck up to the dispatchers, I really do not know what goes through their heads. But they are out there, watching me. Even when people say it is just normal oversight and that I should just ignore it, I can tell certain drivers are reporting on me, because they go completely out of their way to be where I am. You do not just accidentally end up parked at the exact intersection where I had to detour because of construction, right as the radio crackles with another one of those little comments. It takes coordination to do that. 

So, do they think they have a legitimate reason? They probably tell HR and the union that it is all completely above board, just standard compliance checks. But deep down, they have to know what they are doing. They know it is a targeted campaign against me. They just hide behind the excuse of oversight so they can keep getting away with it, and it just... it drives me absolutely insane that no one else will just look at the facts and see through their little charade.
Do you think it's possible that your beliefs about being tracked could change if you were presented with evidence that contradicted them?

Evidence? I... I don't even know what that would look like. What kind of evidence could possibly contradict what I am physically experiencing every single day? I mean, think about it logistically, Doctor. Who would be providing this so-called evidence? Management? The company? Because they are the ones orchestrating the whole thing! 

I know I keep drilling this into the ground, and I know I've said it a dozen times today, but it is the entire reason I am sitting in this chair. I’m here because dispatch and compliance have been tracking my route changes through the computer system. They own that system! They have administrative access to the whole network. If they wanted to print out a spreadsheet or a log file that magically shows no targeted tracking, they could fake it in five seconds. And those little comments on the radio... what, are they going to play back an edited tape for you to prove they didn't say anything? They control the comms room. They can easily delete or scrub the audio logs where they make those snide remarks about my location. 

It’s just... it’s like you’re asking me if I would stop believing the sky is blue if someone handed me a corporate memo saying it was green. The memo doesn't change the sky. And even when people say it’s just normal oversight—which is exactly what any 'evidence' they manufacture would claim—it doesn't erase what I see out there on the road with my own eyes. I can tell certain drivers are reporting on me. I see them idling at my turnaround points, I see them watching me from their cabs, I see the coordinated timing of it all. You can't give me a piece of paper that proves they weren't there, because I was there, and I saw them! 

So, no. No, I don't think my mind would change, because these aren't just 'beliefs' floating around in my head, they are direct observations of my reality. If you brought me evidence saying none of this was happening, I would just... I would know the evidence was fabricated. Because it would have to be. It's just so exhausting that we're even talking about hypothetical evidence against me, instead of looking at the very real, tangible things they are doing to ruin my life and my career. Why would I trust their evidence over my own survival instincts?
Do you think it's possible that your perception of being tracked is a result of your own mind playing tricks on you, rather than actual events happening?

My mind playing tricks on me? Doctor, honestly, it feels like we are just going in circles here. I mean, I get it. I get why you have to ask that, because you’re a psychiatrist and that’s your job, to figure out if the brain is misfiring or whatever. But you are basically just asking me the same thing you asked five minutes ago about whether my interpretation is wrong, just using different words again. 

You have to understand my position. I'm a professional driver, I have my associate's degree, I know my routes, I know my vehicle, and I know my own mind. If I were just sitting in a dark room imagining things, or if I were half-asleep, maybe. But I am out there on the road, navigating heavy traffic, dealing with tight schedules, completely lucid and awake. My mind has to be sharp just to do my job safely. 

And I know I’ve said this so many times already today, and I’m sorry to keep beating a dead horse, but it’s the entire reason I’m even sitting here in this clinic. I’m here because dispatch and compliance have been tracking my route changes through the computer system. That is a physical, digital reality. It's not a trick of the light, it's not a hallucination. And those little comments on the radio... they are audible. They are coming through a physical speaker into the cab of my truck. How does my mind play a trick that involves a dispatcher pressing a button and making a sarcastic comment about my exact location for everyone on the channel to hear? 

And then there are the other drivers. I talk to people about this, and even when people say it’s just normal oversight, or that I'm just stressed out and seeing things that aren't there... I can tell certain drivers are reporting on me. I can physically see them. I can see them when they pull up next to me at a red light on a detour I wasn't even supposed to be on! My mind isn't conjuring up a ten-ton vehicle idling next to me just to mess with me. They are really there. 

So, no. My mind is not playing tricks on me. My mind is working perfectly fine, and it is picking up on a very real, very coordinated effort to monitor my every move. It's just so incredibly exhausting to sit here and have my sanity questioned when I am the one being harassed. I just wish someone would actually listen to what I'm telling them instead of trying to convince me that my own life isn't real.
Do you think it's possible that you might be misinterpreting the intentions of your coworkers and supervisors?

Misinterpreting their intentions? Doctor, I... I feel like we are just playing a game of semantics now. First it was whether they have a legitimate reason, then it was about evidence, then it was my mind playing tricks on me, and now it's about whether I'm just misunderstanding what they mean by it all. It’s... it’s honestly just exhausting. Really, it is. Because how on earth do you misinterpret a coordinated campaign against you? 

I know I have literally said this to you in almost every single answer today, but I have to keep bringing it back to the facts, because it is the absolute foundation of why I am sitting in this room with you. I am here because dispatch and compliance have been tracking my route changes through the computer system. That is a concrete reality. There is no 'good intention' behind zooming in on my specific truck, watching every single detour I take, and analyzing my movements like I'm some sort of criminal. If their intention was just to do their jobs, they wouldn't be making those little comments on the radio. You don't just accidentally lean on the mic button and make a coded, sarcastic joke about exactly where I am parked or what turn I just missed. You do that because your intention is to let me know you are watching. You do that to intimidate me, to make me feel like I have nowhere to hide. 

And my coworkers? The other drivers on the grid? I mean, I try to be reasonable. I really do. I try to think, 'Oh, maybe Jim just got reassigned,' or 'Maybe Sarah is just taking a different way back to the yard to avoid traffic.' But I'm not stupid. I pay attention to my surroundings. Even when people say it’s just normal oversight, or just a coincidence of the schedule, I can tell certain drivers are reporting on me. I can see it in their body language when we cross paths at the depot. I see them idling at the exact intersections I was forced to detour down, just sitting there in their cabs, watching me pass by. You don't misinterpret a ten-ton truck sitting there waiting for you. Their intention is to keep tabs on me for management, probably to get better routes or favor with the dispatchers. 

So no, I really don't think I'm misinterpreting anything. I think I am the only one actually seeing their intentions for exactly what they are. They want me to crack under the pressure, and it just feels like you're trying to find any possible excuse to make it my fault, or my misunderstanding, instead of holding them accountable for what they are doing to me out there.
Do you think the people tracking you are part of a larger conspiracy?

A larger conspiracy? I mean, I do not know if I would use the word conspiracy, like it is some spy movie with the government or something. That word makes it sound crazy, and I am not crazy, Doctor. I am just a professional dealing with my reality. But if you mean, is it more than just one guy in a headset messing with me? Yes. Absolutely. It has to be.
